title: Probabilistic kernel chooser: quant-aware runtime dispatch for FP8/INT8/FP16
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Motivation: as we expand support for FP8 and INT8 quantized kernels alongside FP16, we need a runtime dispatcher that selects the best kernel variant per-request in a way that balances accuracy guarantees, latency SLOs, and cost. Current approaches are static (model-wide) or rely on simple heuristics that don't account for request shape (sequence length, batch size), KV-cache hit rates, or runtime telemetry. This ticket proposes a probabilistic kernel chooser that uses calibrated quant profiles and a lightweight decision model to dispatch between FP16/FP8/INT8 kernel paths with shadow validation and graceful fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime module 'kernel_chooser' selects a kernel variant per-request using inputs: model_id, layer_profile, seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio, user_slo_hint, and temperature. 2) Offline calibration artifacts (per-layer quant profiles and accuracy budgets) are produced and stored in model metadata. 3) Shadow-run validation demonstrates no more than 0.5% degradation on the critical eval set when choosing quantized kernels at the configured policy thresholds. 4) Rollout feature-flagged canary: 5% traffic with full tracing, and a safe fallback to FP16 on policy breach. 5) Console shows per-kernel latency p50/p95 and accuracy drift metrics per model and per release.
description_of_solution: Two-stage approach: (A) Offline calibration: run a calibration harness that generates per-layer FP8 and INT8 profiles (scale factors, per-channel MSE/KL, dynamic range histograms) and produces an accuracy-cost curve for each candidate quant format. Save these as 'quant_profile' blobs attached to the model bundle. Also run a small eval suite (representative prompts + quant-sensitive prompts) to measure end-to-end generation drift and token-level KL. Produce a per-model 'accuracy budget' threshold for allowed drift.
runtime_design_notes: (B) Runtime kernel chooser: lightweight policy that accepts the offline profiles and runtime signals and outputs a kernel variant token stream plan. Core components: - feature extractor: pulls seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio, recent_latency_hist, model_version, and request-level accuracy_budget_hint. - decision model: default is a calibrated logistic regression with coefficients derived from offline replay; falls back to a rule-based fallback if telemetry is missing. - probabilistic sampling: when multiple kernels are acceptable within accuracy budget, sample between them based on cost-weighted probability to collect coverage data. - shadow-run: selected quantized path is shadow-run alongside FP16 for a configurable fraction of tokens/requests to measure divergence without impacting user latency. - fallback rules: immediate fallback to FP16 on kernel error, excessive latency, or drift beyond configured thresholds. - caching: cache per-model+shape decisions for N minutes to avoid decision overhead on hot paths.
implementation_tasks: - Implement calibration harness improvements to emit per-layer quant_profile JSONs and a compact accuracy curve CSV. - Add model-metadata storage hooks in model registry for quant_profile blobs. - Build 'kernel_chooser' service/module with C++ runtime shim + Python control-plane bindings. - Instrument lightweight telemetry keys: kernel_variant, chooser_version, chosen_prob, shadow_drift_metric, fallback_reason. - Add console dashboards and tracing hooks for per-kernel latency, memory usage, and shadow-run drift. - Add e2e tests: 1) replay harness to validate chooser decisions on stored traces; 2) integration tests that force fallback scenarios. - Prepare rollout: feature flag, canary config (5% -> 25% -> 100%), automated abort criteria.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Risk: shadow-run adds CPU/GPU overhead if naively implemented; mitigate by sampling and token-level shadowing. - Risk: overfitting chooser to calibration dataset; mitigate by diversifying eval prompt sets and online monitoring. - Complexity vs. benefit: introduces a decision layer which can add latency; mitigate via caching and very small decision models. - Safety: always allow deterministic fallback to FP16 for regulatory/accuracy-critical tenants. - Dependency on quality of quant profiles: if calibration is poor, chooser will make bad decisions; require calibration quality gates.
observability_and_metrics: Must surface: per-kernel p50/p95/p99 latency, per-kernel throughput, GPU memory usage, shadow-run token-level KL and edit distance, chooser decision distribution, fallback counts and reasons, per-model accuracy drift over time. Export metrics with labels: model_id, release, kernel_variant, chooser_version.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Internal dogfood: enable for 10% of low-risk orgs with full tracing and alerts. 3) Canary: 5% public traffic. Monitor drift and latency for 72h. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with automated rollback triggers (drift>0.5% on critical eval suite OR kernel_error_rate>0.1%). 5) Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window for silent regressions.
comments: 2026-02-20 Sofia Alvarez: Initial ticket created after spike showing variability in per-layer quant sensitivity. Proposed probabilistic approach to gather more signal while protecting accuracy.
2026-02-25 Ravi Patel: Reviewed offline calibration requirements. Suggest adding per-channel KL and a small adversarial prompt set to surface brittle layers.

2026-03-02 Priya Nair (MLR): Concern about shadow-run cost; proposed token-level shadowing with 1% sampling and request-level shadowing for 0.1% of requests. Also suggested adding deterministic fallback tag for enterprise customers.
2026-03-07 Design review (Maya Chen): Suggest UI hooks in Console to expose chooser rationale on a per-request basis for debugging (e.g., 'chosen because: low-seq-length & high-kv-hit').
2026-03-12 Infra note (Jared Kim): Will need small kernel registry changes to expose memory footprints and aligned-alloc constraints to the chooser. I'll follow up with a prep PR.
2026-03-14 Ravi Patel: Updated ticket with rollout thresholds and acceptance criteria. Assigned to me for implementation planning.
